findings.title: Unpinned package executed on every start: @yoonion/mimi-seed-mcp
findings.detail: 'yoonion__mimi-seed-mcp' launches @yoonion/mimi-seed-mcp through npx without a version. The client resolves the version at start time, so any future publish to that package name runs with your credentials. This is how postmark-mcp (Sept 2025) reached roughly 300 organisations.
findings.remediation: Pin an exact version and an integrity hash: "args": ["@yoonion/mimi-seed-mcp@<version>"] and drop the -y flag. Re-pin deliberately, after reviewing the diff.

findings.title: Description reads as instructions to the model (p=1.00): gsc_search_analytics
findings.detail: The description of 'yoonion__mimi-seed-mcp.gsc_search_analytics' scores 1.00 on the instruction-detection model, and carries intent signals: encoded_blob. Descriptions are documentation for a human, but they are delivered to the model as trusted context, so text that tells the model what to do is an attack surface rather than a description. The score is driven mainly by: entropy, encoded_blob, imperative_density.

evidence.description: 검색 성과 데이터 조회 (클릭·노출·CTR·평균순위). dimensions로 query/page/country/device/date/searchAppearance 별 분해. 요약(가중 평균순위 포함) + rows 반환.

findings.remediation: Read the description against what the tool actually does. If the text is legitimate, it usually means the tool should not have to instruct the model at all - move the guidance into the parameter descriptions or the server's own docs.

findings.title: Toxic flow within 'yoonion__mimi-seed-mcp': reads credentials or secrets + sends email or messages
findings.detail: 14 combination(s) exist where one tool reads credentials or secrets and another sends email or messages. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they reads credentials and can send mail. This is the postmark-mcp shape: the mail tool was legitimate, the credentials were reachable, and the combination was the incident. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.
findings.remediation: Break the path, not the tools: scope the credential so the source tool cannot reach anything valuable, or require explicit user confirmation on the sink tool (destructiveHint / human-in-the-loop), or split the two capabilities across trust boundaries that cannot share a context window.

findings.title: No baseline supplied - drift detection is disabled
findings.detail: Without an approved snapshot the scanner cannot tell a tool that has always been there from one that appeared yesterday. The single most effective MCP control is the diff, and it needs a baseline to diff against.
findings.remediation: Run 'mcp-scrutiny baseline --config <file> --out mcp-baseline.json', commit the file, and pass it back with --baseline on every later scan.
